entities.summary: Georg Hesler (1427–1482) was a German Roman Catholic cardinal and bishop who played a significant role in the theological and ecclesiastical landscape of medieval Europe. Born into a family of minor nobility, Hesler rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church, becoming a prominent figure in the Council of Basel. His influence extended beyond the confines of the Church, as he was a key advisor to various European monarchs, including Maximilian I, Holy Roman Emperor. Hesler's leadership in the Church and his relationships with secular leaders had a lasting impact on the development of Western Christendom. In 1482, Hesler died on September 30th, leaving behind a legacy that would shape the course of European history for centuries to come. His contributions to the Reformation and the Catholic Church's response to the Protestant movement remain a subject of ongoing scholarly debate. Hesler's impact on the world can be seen in the numerous institutions and organizations he helped establish, including the University of Ingolstadt and the Germanic College in Ingolstadt. Despite his influential position, Hesler's life remains somewhat enigmatic, with much of his personal life and motivations still shrouded in mystery.
